subject: Olympus AI — Dedicated capacity: scaling & isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@olympus.ai>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Olympus AI — Dedicated capacity: scaling & isolation follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we have clear next steps.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Production latency spikes on long-context inference (p95 > 1.2s) during batch scoring windows.
- Data isolation constraints for clinical datasets — needs tenant-level GPU isolation and strict VPC-only egress.
- Peak throughput variability: bursts of up to 80k tokens/min for short periods, baseline ~8k tokens/min.

Primary goals we heard:
1) Reserve a dedicated pool that guarantees isolation and predictable tail latency for customer-facing endpoints.
2) Keep unit cost under $0.006/token (current target) while handling burst windows.
3) 99.9% uptime SLA with an escalation path and regional failover.

Preliminary technical proposal (high level):
- Dedicated pool: 6x A-100 equivalent GPUs reserved (1-zone), with optional burst capacity to add 2 GPUs for ~3–6 minute windows.
- Isolation: physical pool tenancy + VPC private endpoints, with KMS integration for keys.
- Scaling plan: steady autoscale floor at 6 GPUs, policy to add +2 for 10% CPU/KV saturation events with automated fallback to a slightly lower-capacity but compatible model variant if burst cannot be met.
- SLA targets: 99.9% monthly uptime; P95 latency target < 0.9s for standard requests and documented fallbacks for long-context (>8k tokens) cases.

Costs & timeline (ballpark):
- Monthly reserved cost estimate (starting point): ~$85k/month (6x reserved) + consumption-based burst usage. Exact pricing to be validated by finance.
- Typical onboarding timeline: 6–8 weeks (env setup, security review, smoke POC).

Attachments: OLYMPUS_MA_plan_v1.pdf (proposal), redwood-dedicated-prelim-sla.pdf (SLA summary).

Next steps (action owners):
- Olympus: confirm whether regulatory review requires on-prem package or VPC-only (Alice) — due 2026-08-12.
- Redwood: produce a top-level capacity estimate and simple POC scope (Avery) — due 2026-08-11.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with infra and security (Marissa) — propose 60–75 minute session.

If that matches your notes, I’ll schedule the deep-dive and share a draft reserved capacity SOW.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: [OLYMPUS_MA_plan_v1.pdf (6 pages), redwood-dedicated-prelim-sla.pdf (3 pages)]

Subject: Re: Olympus AI — Dedicated capacity: scaling & isolation follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. This aligns well with what I took away. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock dates: 

1) Burst behavior: when you say +2 GPUs for bursts, is that a hard cap we can increase for short windows? We sometimes see ~5–7 minute spikes in usage for batch scoring and want to avoid queueing.
2) Model fallbacks: we need a documented degradation path that preserves clinical QA — how do you guarantee output-stability if we drop to a lower-capacity variant?
3) Security: our security team will want a packet capture policy and confirmation that audit logs (read/write) are retained for 12 months. Can you confirm retention and access controls?

We’re broadly comfortable with the proposed pool size; the main gating factor for procurement is the security scope and a firm cost number.

Available for the deep-dive on 8/12 after 10:00 PT or 8/13 morning. Also looping in security@olympus.ai for the compliance questions.

Thanks — Alice
Head of Platform — Olympus AI

Alice — thanks, and great questions. Quick responses inline and a couple proposed slots for the technical deep-dive.

On Aug 10, 2026 at 9:02 AM Alice Park <alice.park@olympus.ai> wrote:
> 1) Burst behavior: when you say +2 GPUs for bursts, is that a hard cap we can increase for short windows?

Short answer: we can configure a burst ceiling higher than +2, but for reserved pricing we typically size the burst policy conservatively to avoid runaway costs. For the POC we can enable a test mode that allows +4 GPUs for 10-minute windows so you can observe queuing behavior.

> 2) Model fallbacks: we need a documented degradation path that preserves clinical QA — how do you guarantee output-stability if we drop to a lower-capacity variant?

We recommend pinning a quantized compat model as the fallback and running a small eval suite of ~200 critical prompts to verify behavioral parity within an agreed delta. Rishi will lead the eval design; we’ll include eval results as part of the POC acceptance criteria.

> 3) Security: packet capture policy and audit retention

We retain admin and access logs for 12 months by default. Network-level packet captures are not collected by default in hosted mode, but for Dedicated we can enable scoped packet captures for the POC window and store them behind customer KMS with a 12-month retention policy. I’ll loop in our compliance lead if Olympus wants to extend retention beyond that.

Deep-dive slots (60–75m):

- Fri 2026-08-13 09:00–10:15 PT
